_readme: Scoring checks used by the Internal ML model. They look at the card TEXT ONLY, never at performance. Weights and wording are first guesses written while analysing one brand: they are NOT validated. The Training data tab shows, across brands, which checks hold; the Gold set tab scores them against human ratings. Tune them from that evidence.

watch.b: No price, amount, code or benefit appears in the text, so the reader cannot tell what they get.
watch.rec: **Name the offer with a number, price or code** in the title or the first line of the description.

watch.h: Offer not quantified in the text
watch.b: A benefit is named but no number, price or code appears in the text. A figure that lives only in the image disappears if the image does not load.
watch.rec: **Name the offer with a number, price or code** in the title or the first line of the description.

watch.h: A chance, not a sure benefit
watch.b: Language such as win, chance, lucky or giveaway asks a mass audience to act for an uncertain reward.
watch.rec: **Replace chance-based language with a sure benefit,** or state the entry rule and the prize up front.

watch.b: A deadline is pressed but no benefit, price or code is named, so the urgency has nothing behind it.
watch.rec: **Pair every deadline with a concrete benefit.**

watch.h: A floor or ceiling, not an offer
watch.b: Wording such as min or up to tells the reader the worst or best case, not what they get.
watch.rec: **State the actual offer** rather than a minimum or a maximum.

watch.b: The description runs past the point where a reader will finish it.
watch.rec: **Cut the description** to the offer, the rule and one action.

watch.b: Several variables raise the chance that one renders blank or wrong.
watch.rec: **Use fewer variables** and test that each renders for every recipient.

watch.b: Heavy capitals and repeated exclamation marks can read as noise.
The text asks the reader to type or send a reply as well as tapping the button, which splits intent.
watch.rec: **Keep one action per card.** Do not ask for a typed reply next to a button.

watch.b: The title is short and holds no number, so the part most likely to be read says little.

works.b: A price, amount, percentage or quantity appears in the text itself.
A code gives the reader something specific to use.
The whole card text is brief enough to read in one glance.
The text asks for one thing, the button.

dos: Lead with the most specific offer: a price, a code or a named benefit
Pair any deadline with a concrete benefit
Make the image and the text say the same thing
Keep the rule and the deadline within the first two lines
Use one offer and one clear action per card
Put any figure that matters in the text, not only in the image
donts: Use sweepstakes language for mass sends
Use a minimum or a maximum in place of the offer
Draw a button into the image
Stack several propositions or conditions in one card
Send repeated promos to the same audience without a frequency cap
